summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey puts AI use in transportation and warehousing, NAICS 48-49, at 13.0% of firms in the latest period, against 7.9% in the prior period. The question asked is whether the business used AI in the last two weeks, and the survey has been asking it since September 2023. That is the only measured adoption figure in this material, and it covers the whole sector rather than any single mode.

Where the sources show deployment at scale is fleet operations. Samsara describes a connected operations platform used by 20,000+ operations, with AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching and drowsiness detection, and it credits those technologies with 380,000+ accidents prevented. C.H. Robinson frames its offering as autonomous logistics orchestration, where the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes and improves continuously across every shipment, and its page carries an AI assistant that helps visitors explore shipping options. Aurora describes the Aurora Driver as hardware and software backed by verifiable AI, integrated into fleets, with a pilot hauling freight between Fort Worth and El Paso in a hybrid model pairing Werner professional drivers with the Aurora Driver, and integration into the Volvo VNL Autonomous.

Aviation and maritime move more slowly and are gated by regulators. Airbus says it works toward a decarbonised, connected and autonomous future for aerospace, translating innovative ideas into breakthroughs through an open innovation ecosystem. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out the agency's vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, with an action plan, conceptual guidance deliverables and anticipated rulemaking, and it is a living document amended once a year. The IMO adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, a goal-based framework that is voluntary guidance, technology-neutral, and designed to facilitate a future transition into a mandatory instrument. The IMO states that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely-controlled, though trials have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible. Wärtsilä lists AI-driven predictive analytics among the tools it offers customers for decarbonisation.

The vendor layer concentrates in a few named players. Samsara counts 20,000+ operations on its platform. The American Trucking Associations describes itself as the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking, with more than 37,000 members and a federation of 50 state trucking associations, and it works to influence government policies affecting the industry. Wärtsilä describes itself as a global leader in technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The curated points on this site add that Maersk applies AI across global route and port-congestion prediction, that Mobileye supplies the computer-vision stack in driver-assist systems worldwide, and that Palantir, tracked in this site's directory, is used by airlines and rail operators for fleet and crew optimization. This site's own Robotics Models section tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, refreshed daily, which is where vision-language-action and control models of this kind are catalogued.

The ROI evidence the sources report is mostly vendor-reported and operational. Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented is the largest single claim, tied to safety technology rather than to a financial return. Aurora's page carries customer testimony that early pilot results are impressive, particularly autonomous hauling between Fort Worth and El Paso, that autonomous trucks will help grow business and give drivers better lives by handling lengthier and less desirable routes, and that freight volumes are projected to grow five fold between 2010 and 2050, making autonomous transport a necessity rather than an innovation. Waymo's safety hub is described here as the most complete public evidence base from an autonomous vehicle operator, with published methodology and crash-rate comparisons, and Waymo states it supports the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy by advancing safer vehicles and safer speeds, alongside the Vision Zero Network's goal of eliminating traffic fatalities and severe injuries.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material points to a split. The measured base is still small, at 13.0% of transportation and warehousing firms per the Census Bureau, and the deployments the sources describe in most detail are telematics, driver monitoring, predictive maintenance and freight matching, where the operational case is concrete. Full autonomy is further out and is explicitly gated: EASA's roadmap is a living document with rulemaking still anticipated, the IMO's MASS Code is voluntary guidance that may become mandatory, and the IMO notes no internationally trading SOLAS cargo ship currently operates autonomously or remotely. The American Trucking Associations is the body tracking policy for autonomous freight, and the FAA's innovation work and EASA's roadmap are described here as the regulatory record for AI flight systems, automated risk management and eVTOL certification, with nothing flying commercially without them.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The World of AI catalogues what it calls the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each one's licence, downloads and release date. It says the list is refreshed daily and comes from the Hub's public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page gives a last-verified date of 30 September 2026. It also states that its other sections ,  among them state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary and a tools directory ,  are built from the same database and rebuilt daily from primary sources.
